technique.how: Inspect the supine abdomen from the foot and side of the bed for generalised or asymmetric bulging; compare with the patient's baseline. Percuss all quadrants: tympany suggests gas-filled bowel (obstruction/ileus), dullness suggests fluid, a distended bladder or mass; check suprapubic dullness for retention. Measure girth if serial assessment is needed.
technique.prerequisites: Expose from xiphoid to pubis; empty the bladder or note its status; know the surgical history.

interpretation.positive_finding: New tympanitic distension in a patient with pain and vomiting substantially raises the likelihood of bowel obstruction; tense distension with rising airway pressures or oliguria raises concern for abdominal compartment syndrome.
interpretation.negative_finding: A flat abdomen makes complete small-bowel obstruction less likely but does not exclude proximal or early obstruction, perforation or ischaemia.
interpretation.pitfalls: Obesity, ascites, pregnancy, a full bladder and chronic constipation all cause distension without obstruction; proximal SBO may produce little distension. Inspection alone cannot distinguish ileus from mechanical obstruction.
interpretation.changes_what: Distension with pain/vomiting or prior surgery: obtain CT abdomen and surgical review; tense distension with oliguria/high airway pressures: measure bladder pressure for ACS.

sources.citation: Taylor MR, Lalani N. Adult small bowel obstruction. Acad Emerg Med. 2013;20(6):528-544.

Eskelinen M, Ikonen J, Lipponen P. Contributions of history-taking, physical examination, and computer assistance to diagnosis of acute small-bowel obstruction. A prospective study of 1333 patients with acute abdominal pain. Scand J Gastroenterol. 1994;29(8):715-721.

Bohner H, Yang Q, Franke C, Verreet PR, Ohmann C. Simple data from history and physical examination help to exclude bowel obstruction and to avoid radiographic studies in patients with acute abdominal pain. Eur J Surg. 1998;164(10):777-784.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of distension to exclude obstruction in early, proximal or closed-loop obstruction, or in patients with an ostomy or recent laparotomy.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Distension with peritonism, fever, tachycardia or lactate rise suggests strangulation or perforation: immediate surgical consultation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Inspection for distension is subjective; agreement is unreported in the SBO meta-analysis, and obesity reduces reliability.

extraction_notes: Taylor & Lalani 2013 (PMID 23758299) pool sens/spec/LR for distension, but the article is not open access and the abstract gives no distension-specific numbers, so the pooled LR could not be quoted with a location. Bohner 1998 abstract names distended abdomen among the six most sensitive variables without numbers. Only visible number is the Eskelinen 1994 relative risk (13.1), entered with sens/spec/LR null since RR is not an LR and no 2x2 is visible. Owner should transcribe Taylor 2013 Table (history/exam) to complete. Eskelinen 1994 (PMID 7973431, Abstract) reports relative risk 13.1 for abdominal distension; removed from estimates[] because RR is not a schema statistic, so status is not_quantified despite pooled data existing in the unreachable Taylor 2013 tables.
